newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies end lower-limit down, hogs gain.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies end lower-limit down, hogs gain.

text.p: CME pork belly futures fully reversed early limit gains and ended lower to down the daily limit of 2.000 cents a lb as storage concerns offset support linked to last week's USDA Cold Storage report, traders said.
August ended limit down at 90.525 cents and February was offered limit down in the closing range, settling 1.975 lower at 83.250. Other months ended 1.550 to 0.050 cent lower.

Commercial selling developed after the inital limit jump on the bullish storage report. Although the data showed belly stocks at 20-year lows for July, February is a long way off and stocks will likely rise by then, traders said.

Floor sources noted that belly traders had been expecting a more bullish report than analysts estimated and the runup at the start provided a selling opportunity. August also eased on the large premium ahead of Tuesday's expiration , they said.

"The fresh market did not respond to the Cold Storage figure the way the futures did, so the fresh and futures market parted company. Secondly, the outside warehouse figure for last week, which is released tomorrow afternoon, is expected to be a lousy number," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.
"Very high prices slowed down the usage rate," he said.
USDA put frozen belly stocks at 28.5 million lbs versus estimates of 35.1 million to 38.7 million lbs which sparked the initial limit gains.
Levitt added that last week's CME out-of-town storage data could show movement unchanged after withdrawals started falling behind year-ago withdrawals the past couple of weeks.
Too large a premium of February to cash will also encourage heavy storings especially after recent weakness in cash bellies, traders added.
Hog futures also retreated from early highs but generally held gains at the close.

The storage report showed total pork stocks at 321.5 million lbs versus 408.3 million lbs in storage August 1, 1995. But demand lacked follow through and prices retreated in light dealings. Paring of gains in pork bellies also weighed on sentiment, they said.
Rand Financials bought October late while R.J. O'Brien sold, traders said. In hog options, there was general buying of February 70 to 74 puts, pit sources said.
Hog futures closed 0.275 cent higher to 0.075 lower with October up most at 54.650 cents a lb
